At step k (block column), diagonal block owner (the rank whose row range contains k) factors diagonal tile and then computes the panel L[k:,k] which requires rows k..n. Rows below the owner's chunk belong to other ranks, so owner cannot compute them. Panel computation requires L_kk (available), then L_ik = A_ik * L_kk^{-T} for each i>k. Each rank can compute its own rows' panel entries since it holds A_ik (rows i in its range, column block k). So:\n  1. Owner of diagonal tile factors L_kk, broadcasts L_kk (nb×nb) to all ranks (MPI_Bcast).\n  2. Each rank with rows > k computes its local panel entries L_ik = A_ik L_kk^{-T} for i in its rows (i>=k+1), applies to its own data.\n  3. Each rank broadcasts its local panel rows to all (MPI_Allgatherv) so all ranks have full L[k:,k].\n  4. Each rank updates its local rows: for rows i in my rows with i>k, for all j in (k+1 .. i): A_ij -= L_ik * L_jk^T. This needs L_jk for j possibly owned by other ranks — available from the allgather panel. So each rank computes full update for its own row block: O(rowChunk * n * nb) per step. Total work is distributed by rows but the update A_ij for j<i uses panel entries of rows j that are replicated. Fine.\n\nWork distribution: rank with rows chunk ~ n/np. The last rank owns the bottom rows, does decreasing work; first rank's rows get factored early and then its trailing update is small.
